findings.summary: Tier 2 plans every month in [EDGAR_FLOOR_START, asof] regardless of persisted state, and the only gate before those ~198 rows become authoritative is validateEdgarBatch, which accepts any finite non-negative integer including 0 — the value parseEdgarCount returns verbatim for an HTTP-200 empty result set. No comparison against the persisted floor existed on the submit path, and the write clobbers via ON CONFLICT (date, indicator) DO UPDATE SET value, source. One EDGAR FTS index rebuild rewrites the full 2010-to-present series and its provenance; applyRawFloorSeed only fills MISSING dates, so no in-system repair existed.

runProducerOnce invoked runAnalytics once per research tool, so fetchResearchInputs — and its live EDGAR sweep — ran twice per cycle; only the late-cycle-signals branch persists the result, so the first sweep's ~200 requests (and any degrade it observed) were discarded.

`tier` was added to EdgarRefreshOutcome but omitted from the orchestrator log line and never persisted, so producer downtime across the single full-sweep weekday (or a weekday-only PRODUCER_RESEARCH_CRON) disables reconciliation indefinitely with no catch-up and no alarm.
A degraded Tier 2 sweep suppressed the daily late-cycle signal Tier 1 would have published, even though the incremental data was fine and cheap to fetch.

Both real-API+Postgres suites were repinned to Sunday asof values and their boundedness guards deleted (edgar1.length < 10, the startdtOf(r.url) >= "2026-01-01" loop, floorAfterRun1.length < 200), leaving the incremental tier — 6 of 7 production runs — with zero end-to-end coverage while the suite stayed green.

extract/edgar-fetch-plan.ts's header claimed the #108 seed artifact is "untouched by this module" while Tier 2 rewrites its rows weekly, flipping source seed→live; repopulateEdgarSeed's `rejected` counter consequently reports the entire artifact as rejected after the first full sweep.
This very artifact recorded a pass pinned to a commit absent from main's history and to the wrong merge-base — corrected by the superseded_verdict record above.

clean_areas: Tier-selection determinism/replay-safety: selectEdgarRefreshTier(asOf) reads only its asOf string argument via getUTCDay() on `${asOf}T00:00:00Z` — no Date.now()/wall-clock call anywhere in the function.

No tier-decision drift between call sites: analytics/index.ts sizes the deadline from selectEdgarRefreshTier(asof) and access/data-source.ts passes that same asof string unchanged into the refresh, which recomputes the tier from the identical input — the same pure function on the same string, so they cannot disagree.

No duplicate/double-counted rows across a tier switch: the durable write path is a true upsert keyed on (date, indicator), and the in-memory mergeSeries is a Map keyed by date, so a Tier-1-then-Tier-2 sequence is idempotent by construction on both.
Whole-batch-degrade honesty model applies identically to both tiers: refreshEdgarIncremental and validateEdgarBatch are single shared code paths; only the plan array's origin differs.

Ordering, uniqueness, positional plan-to-result correspondence, and deadline propagation into per-request aborts all hold. PR #464's fidelity reference still reproduces mna_pct at maxDiff=0 through the tier-'full' path.
